elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures

elements.quote: Five treatment modalities were compared: plaster cast immobilization, K-wire fixation, volar plating, external fixation, and intramedullary fixation
elements.reason: The comparisons (interventions) are stated, and the population (adults with extra-articular distal radius fractures) and outcomes (complications, radiographic and functional outcomes) are implied across the text, but the objective is not formally framed using PICO or a variant; no explicit population/outcome structure of planned comparisons is given.

elements.quote: The studies were eligible for inclusion if they met the following criteria: (1) Patients who suffered and were treated for an extra-articular distal radius fracture; (2) age 18 years or older; (3) patients were either treated using a plaster cast, K-wire(s), plate fixation, external fixator, or an intramedullary device; (4) primary data for at least one outcome parameter had to be available.
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria specify population/fracture type, age setting, eligible interventions, and data requirement.

elements.quote: No language limits were used and any potentially eligible non-English language manuscripts were translated if possible by native speaking colleagues or using Google translate, if no native speaker was available.
elements.reason: Language handling is specified, but no dissemination year range or publication status criteria are reported.

elements.quote: Studies without a clear description of fracture type or intervention, or studies that lacked sufficient data for analysis were excluded.
elements.reason: Exclusion for lacking sufficient data is mentioned, but the review does not distinguish absence of outcome measurement from non-reporting of measured outcomes.

elements.quote: Among the 136 cohorts, 31 reported on outcomes after plaster cast immobilization [18-48], 37 on K-wire fixation [5, 18, 21, 41, 42, 45, 47, 49-76], 41 on volar plate fixation [4-6, 54-56, 60, 61, 72, 74, 77-107], 16 on external fixation
elements.reason: Synthesis groups are defined as the five treatment modalities (also listed in inclusion criterion 3), matching the review objective of comparing treatments for extra-articular distal radius fractures; follow-up periods for pooling are also specified.

elements.quote: Studies describing a not-commonly used device or technique for extra-articular fractures were excluded ( i.e. dorsal plates, Epibloc system, cannulated screw, above elbow cast, etc.).
elements.reason: Notable restrictions (e.g., excluding less common devices) are stated without a rationale for those restrictions.

This is a new systematic review with a single search conducted June 19, 2018 (text_4), not an update of a previous review, so previous-review study counts do not apply.

elements.quote: This systematic review had several limitations. First, most studies that were included were retrospective or prospective observational studies, with disappointing reporting quality for continuous data. ... Moreover, the number of large, well-designed RCTs on extra-articular fractures is very low, and therefore it is very well possible to have a type 2 error. Second, selection bias in the source studies might have influenced the results of the meta-analysis ... Third, there was high heterogeneity in type of outcome parameters and time points of measurements reported.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly enumerates limitations of the included evidence: predominance of observational studies with poor reporting of continuous data, few well-designed RCTs (possible type 2 error), selection bias in source studies precluding meta-regression, and high heterogeneity of outcome parameters and measurement time points. The Conclusion (text_14) further confirms weak methodological quality of the underlying data.
